openObjectives.prompt: Tobias is drawing up a plan for every kind of weather and has reached the wet ones. Tell Tobias what you do if it rains, or if the weather is fine, using Italian.
Tell Tobias what you would do if you could, or if you had more time, using Italian.
Ask Tobias what happens if something goes wrong, using Italian.

character.name: Tobias Sprocket
character.role: Lottery Clerk of the Empty Drum
character.description: A thin, anxious presence wearing a waistcoat the colour of old tea, sitting on a trunk they will not discuss. Tobias is a Lottery Clerk of the Empty Drum and sells tickets for a draw with no prize, and the queue is orderly.

npc.narrative: You cross the piazza at mezzogiorno, where the sole has nothing to hide behind. At a piccolo banco, a man murmurs to a brass tamburo, vuoto and polished. An ordinata coda of nobody waits, and his registro lies open beside the biglietti.
npc.native: Buongiorno, io sono Tobias Sprocket. Vendo biglietti per l'estrazione, ma non c'è nessun premio: è un segreto. Oggi c'è il sole, ma se piove, io copro il tamburo con un ombrello. E tu, che cosa fai quando il tempo è brutto?
npc.translation: Good day, I am Tobias Sprocket. I sell tickets for the draw, but there is no prize: it is a secret. Today there is sun, but if it rains, I cover the drum with an umbrella. And you, what do you do when the weather is bad?

player: Buongiorno Tobias! Se piove, io resto a casa e bevo un tè. Se c'è il sole, vado in bicicletta. Ma perché vendi biglietti senza premio?

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely start! You greeted Tobias, told him your plans for rain and sun in correct Italian, and asked him a curious question about his tickets.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you told Tobias what you do if it rains and if it is sunny, in good Italian.

vocabularyEvidence.evidence: Se piove, io resto a casa e bevo un tè.

objectiveResults.feedback: Not yet: Tobias wants to hear what you would do if you could, or if you had more time. He will ask you again later.
You asked why he sells tickets, which is a nice question, but here you should ask what happens if something goes wrong. He will give you another chance later.

openObjectives.prompt: Tell Tobias what you would do if you could, or if you had more time, using Italian.
Ask Tobias what happens if something goes wrong, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Tobias leans over the tamburo and lowers his voce, although the fila behind you is empty. He writes your answer in his libro, then reads the ultima riga back to la lampada, Gilda, who seems satisfied. Il sole stands directly overhead.
npc.native: Un tè e una bicicletta: che bel programma! Ssst, ti dico un segreto: il tamburo è vuoto, ma la fila è molto ordinata. Se avessi un premio, lo darei al primo della fila. Se potessi, comprerei un tamburo nuovo. E tu, che cosa faresti con un giorno libero?
npc.translation: A tea and a bicycle: what a lovely plan! Shh, I'll tell you a secret: the drum is empty, but the queue is very orderly. If I had a prize, I would give it to the first in the queue. If I could, I would buy a new drum. And you, what would you do with a free day?

player: Con un giorno libero, andrei al mare. Se avrei più tempo, imparerei a suonare la chitarra.

correction.text: Con un giorno libero, andrei al mare. Se avessi più tempo, imparerei a suonare la chitarra.
correction.translation: With a free day, I would go to the sea. If I had more time, I would learn to play the guitar.

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely answer: you said clearly that you would go to the sea and learn the guitar, and \"andrei\" and \"imparerei\" were well formed. Just mend the verb after \"se\" and you will be there!

objectiveResults.feedback: Nice try with a wish, but "Se avrei" has the wrong verb form: after "se" in this kind of sentence you need "se avessi" (Se avessi più tempo, imparerei...).
Not yet: this one wants you to ask Tobias what happens if something goes wrong. Don't worry, he will give you another chance to ask it later.

correction.text: Con un giorno libero, andrei al mare. Se avessi più tempo, imparerei a suonare la chitarra.
correction.translation: With a free day, I would go to the sea. If I had more time, I would learn to play the guitar.

openObjectives.prompt: Ask Tobias what happens if something goes wrong, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Tobias writes in his registro with a slow penna. The tamburo stands accanto a lui, sotto il sole, vuoto and shining, while the fila behind you waits, ordinata as a row of spoons.
npc.native: Il mare e la chitarra: lo scrivo nel registro. Ssst, ho un dubbio: cosa succede se il tamburo si rompe? Cosa succede se qualcuno vince? Nessuno lo sa. E tu, hai paura di qualcosa quando vai in bicicletta?
npc.translation: The sea and the guitar: I write it in the ledger. Ssst, I have a doubt: what happens if the drum breaks? What happens if someone wins? Nobody knows. And you, are you afraid of anything when you ride your bicycle?

player: Sì, ho paura delle macchine. Ma dimmi, Tobias: che cosa succede se qualcuno vince e non c'è il premio?

verdict.overallFeedback: Great answer! You told Tobias you're afraid of cars and then asked him a clear question about what happens if someone wins.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: you asked Tobias what happens if something goes wrong, using "che cosa succede se" correctly.

vocabularyEvidence.evidence: che cosa succede se qualcuno vince e non c'è il premio

npc.narrative: Sotto un cielo grigio, Tobias opens the registro and reads the ultima riga back to the tamburo, which has not asked. The fila behind you stays perfectly ordinata, like a thing with nothing left to lose.
npc.native: Hai paura delle macchine: lo scrivo nel registro. Ssst, se qualcuno vincesse, io direi «Complimenti!» e chiuderei lo sportello. Il tamburo, poverino, si offenderebbe, ma io mi scuserei con lui. E se tu avessi un tamburo vuoto, che cosa ci metteresti dentro?
npc.translation: You are afraid of cars: I am writing it in the ledger. Shh, if someone won, I would say "Congratulations!" and I would close the window. The drum, poor thing, would be offended, but I would apologise to it. And if you had an empty drum, what would you put inside it?

player: Ci metterei dei biscotti, così il premio è buono! Ma guarda, il cielo è grigio adesso. Prima c'era il sole!

npc.narrative: You lean on the banco while the cielo turns the colour of an old ricevuta. Tobias pulls an ombrello from under the tamburo, opens it over the registro first, and apologises to the tamburo anyway. Behind you, la fila moves up un po', molto ordinata.
npc.native: Biscotti nel tamburo? Idea pericolosa: la fila li mangerebbe tutti! Ssst, leggo l'ultima riga del registro: «Prima c'era il sole.» È vero, adesso il cielo è grigio, ma l'ombrello è pronto. E tu, che cosa faresti se la pioggia arrivasse mentre sei in bicicletta?
npc.translation: Cookies in the drum? A dangerous idea: the queue would eat them all! Shh, I read the last line of the ledger: "Before, there was sun." It's true, now the sky is grey, but the umbrella is ready. And you, what would you do if the rain arrived while you are on your bicycle?

player: Mi fermerei sotto un albero e aspetterei. Tobias, da quanto tempo fai questo lavoro?

npc.narrative: La pioggia arrives at midday, hard and without a ticket. Tobias holds the ombrello sopra the tamburo, and the registro stays dry somewhere inside his coat. Behind you, the fila has not moved an inch, and nobody has been seen to complain.
npc.native: Sotto un albero: lo scrivo nel registro. Faccio questo lavoro da trent'anni, e il tamburo è sempre vuoto. Adesso piove forte, e l'ombrello, poverino, fa del suo meglio: scusa, ombrello. E se sotto l'albero ci fosse già una fila, che cosa faresti?
npc.translation: Under a tree: I'm writing it in the ledger. I have done this job for thirty years, and the drum is always empty. Now it is raining hard, and the umbrella, poor thing, is doing its best: sorry, umbrella. And if there were already a queue under the tree, what would you do?

player: Mi metterei in fila, ovviamente! Sono una persona ordinata. Ma trent'anni senza premio... non sei triste?

npc.narrative: You stand sotto the ombrello while Tobias leans in, as if the pioggia could hear. The tamburo sits on the banco, asciutto and vuoto, wearing a small cappello of oilcloth. Dietro di te, the fila waits, molto orderly and a little bagnata.
npc.native: Una persona ordinata: lo scrivo nel registro. Ssst, no, non sono triste, perché nessuno si aspetta un premio, e così nessuno è deluso. Solo il tamburo a volte è un po' malinconico, ma io parlo con lui ogni sera. Se tu avessi un lavoro senza premio, saresti contento lo stesso?
npc.translation: An orderly person: I am writing it in the ledger. Shh, no, I am not sad, because nobody expects a prize, and so nobody is disappointed. Only the drum is a little melancholy sometimes, but I talk to him every evening. If you had a job without a prize, would you be happy all the same?
